candidates.text: The orchestrator's own ad hoc ORCH-* test-runner health-check commands are bound by the exact same strict positional command grammar as agent-requested commands (e.g. a bare 'python -m pytest -q' with no positional target is command_rejected, not silently accepted). Unlike an agent's rejected command -- which halts the phase -- a rejection of the orchestrator's own authored command is the orchestrator's own authoring mistake: retain the rejection as evidence, then correct the command and reissue it under a fresh command_id rather than escalating or blocking the run.

An evidence-retention bridge that independently re-verifies an agent's self-reported affirmative observation (e.g. retain_architect_obsidian_reads re-reading an Architect's claimed mcp__obsidian__read_note) should classify a non-affirmative self-reported status (connector_unavailable, not_found, etc.) as a distinct 'not_applicable' outcome rather than attempting any independent re-check for it -- there is nothing affirmative to corroborate, and attempting one anyway would risk manufacturing evidence the original observation never made.
